title: Built-in web terminal in DSM, so you don’t have to open SSH
body:
It would be very useful to have a native terminal app inside DSM, accessible from the main menu like any other package.

Sometimes you just need to run a few commands, like checking a service, reading a log or fixing a permission. Today the only way is to enable SSH, connect from an external client, and then remember to disable it again. Opening the SSH port, even for a short time, adds an unnecessary attack surface.

A web-based terminal running inside the DSM session would solve this:

No SSH port to open: everything goes through the existing DSM web session (HTTPS).
Same user, same privileges: the shell runs as the user logged into DSM, with exactly the same rights. No privilege escalation, and sudo only for accounts that are already allowed to use it.
Admin control: access can be granted or denied per user or group through the standard DSM application permissions.
Traceability: sessions and commands can be logged in the DSM Log Center.

This would make day-to-day maintenance faster and more secure, especially for users who manage their NAS remotely and don’t want to expose SSH at all.
